answers.answer: No. Based on pretrained knowledge only, I would not call d1s9za_ (Amyloidogenic design-1) and d1hqja_ (Unnamed design-1) homologous. Both are artificial, designed sequences. SCOPe's evolutionary levels (family and superfamily) assume a common natural ancestor, and designed proteins have none. If SCOPe 2.08 places both domains under the same catch-all or placeholder node for designed proteins, that placement is a classification convenience. It is not evidence of shared ancestry. The names "Amyloidogenic design-1" and "Unnamed design-1" are generic labels, not true protein families. A shared label or node therefore does not support family-level or superfamily-level homology, and it does not show a conserved fold or function either. I could not check the exact sccs strings or the node membership of these two entries, so confirm them in the SCOPe 2.08 browser or parseable files. Even if they do share a node, the shared node would not make them homologous. Any structural resemblance (for example, both being helical) would more plausibly reflect convergent design principles than divergence from a common ancestor. Do not transfer function, amyloid propensity, stability, or a template relationship from one entry to the other without independent structural and experimental evidence. Also do not use one as a representative of the other for homology-based inference.
